Title: Sign-in and sessions
Requirement: Users sign in with e-mail and password and receive a 30-minute access token and a single-use, rotating 7-day refresh token; logout and password reset are supported; self-registration is disabled.

Title: Step-up verification
Requirement: A first-login password change is forced, and sensitive operations require an e-mailed one-time code verified within a short window.

Title: Configurable roles
Requirement: An office administrator manages accounts, roles, role permissions, disciplines and memberships, starting from seeded role templates, without code changes.

Title: Per-person exceptions
Requirement: An administrator grants or denies a single permission to one person, everywhere or on one project, and can see which rule decided each permission.

Title: External-party isolation
Requirement: External participants see only project-scoped data explicitly shared with their party and can never hold certification or access-governance permissions.

Title: Projects
Requirement: Authorised users create, edit and delete projects, with a deletion-impact preview and a configurable consultant approval workflow.

Title: Members and parties
Requirement: Project managers assign members with project roles and organise external parties (client, main contractor, subcontractors).

Title: Dashboards and budget view
Requirement: Users see project summaries, an owner dashboard and action-centre counts; projects hold budget total and spent values, and cost validation requests are reviewed with variance and risk level.

Title: Task management
Requirement: Project managers create, assign, prioritise, reorder and edit tasks with planned and actual dates, durations, disciplines and milestones.

Title: Task execution and review
Requirement: A task starts only from TODO when predecessors are done and no blocker is open; assignees report progress and blockers, submit for review, and reviewers approve, reject with corrections or request clarification.

Title: Dependencies and CPM
Requirement: Tasks are linked by FS, SS, FF or SF dependencies with lag; cycles are rejected; the system provides Gantt data, a connected critical path, delay analysis and schedule shifting.

Title: Document library
Requirement: Members upload, search, download and delete documents through authenticated endpoints and share individual documents with an external party.

Title: File ingestion
Requirement: Uploaded files (PDF, DOC/DOCX, XLS/XLSX, IFC, images, ZIP, TXT) are validated, checksummed, de-duplicated, classified and processed asynchronously; DWG/DXF files are stored but not parsed.

Title: Design changes and requests
Requirement: Engineers propose design changes with cost and schedule impact, linked to a task; reviewers approve, reject or mark them implemented; clients raise owner requests.

Title: IFC processing
Requirement: IFC files are uploaded into model groups and versions and parsed in an isolated process into spatial hierarchy, elements, properties and quantities, with quality checks.

Title: Model-derived suggestions
Requirement: Processing proposes construction tasks per element class and per-storey milestones, flagged for duplicate risk; accepting a suggestion creates the task or milestone.

Title: Revision comparison and impact
Requirement: Two versions of one model group are compared by GlobalId into added, removed, modified and moved elements; impact suggestions are created on linked items or same-discipline tasks and are acknowledged or dismissed.

Title: Coordination findings
Requirement: Structural/service interference candidates are computed from element bounding boxes and can be turned into project issues, ignored or marked false positive.

Title: 3D viewing
Requirement: Viewer geometry is generated server-side per version for display in a 3D web viewer.

Title: Grounded document answers
Requirement: Questions are answered only from documents and files the user may read, with citations to document and page, and a not-found answer when the context is insufficient.

Title: Question routing
Requirement: A question is routed deterministically to structured project data, IFC data or document retrieval, defaulting to documents when unsure.

Title: Rule-based insights and agents
Requirement: Deterministic analyzers produce evidence-carrying findings: five agents (site report, document consistency, revision impact, RFI, schedule risk) on demand, and a model-to-execution alignment score.

Title: Event-driven agent analysis
Requirement: Agents run automatically when domain events occur, under the project manager's authority.

Title: Site reports and evidence
Requirement: Site staff submit daily reports and field evidence with directional photographs; authorised engineers verify or return them; photos are archived by category.

Title: Voice-to-action
Requirement: Spoken Arabic or English is transcribed and analysed; questions are answered; proposed changes become drafts executed only after confirmation and a fresh permission check.

Title: Issues, visits and reminders
Requirement: Issues with severity and status are linked to tasks; site visits are scheduled with participants; reminder rules send automatic reminders.

Title: Messaging
Requirement: Members exchange direct, group, project and contextual messages with acknowledgement, response tracking and forwarding.

Title: Notifications
Requirement: Users are notified in-app, by push (Firebase) and by e-mail; the web client receives live update hints over server-sent events.

Title: Audit and AI history
Requirement: Important actions are recorded in audit logs and domain events; AI-initiated changes are stored with before and after state and can be reverted.

Title: Bilingual interface
Requirement: Web and mobile interfaces are available in English and Arabic with right-to-left layout.

Database-backed rate limits on login, one-time-code sending and verification, and MCP tool calls, correct across several API workers.
Documents, IFC sources, geometry and audio are stored privately and streamed only through authenticated endpoints.
Background jobs are enqueued in the causing transaction, de-duplicated, retried with exponential backoff and reclaimed after a stale heartbeat.
Secondary products (geometry, agents, push, indexing) cannot fail the primary operation that triggered them.
Notifications and realtime events are written in the caller's transaction and delivered only after commit.
IFC parsing is bounded by timeouts, memory caps and vertex limits; uploads are size-limited.
Correct behaviour with several API workers (advisory locks, LISTEN/NOTIFY); HNSW vector index; fleet-wide processing ceiling.
No response-time or throughput target is specified and none was measured.
